files.legend.sop:
@legend.art.draw core.legend
    namespace=art.draw
    version=0.1.0
    imports=core
    imports=kids.common
    imports=kids.shapes
    imports=common.sense
    doc="The drawing board: a scene graph of shapes and things on a fixed canvas"

@art.draw.picture core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="The drawing. The world state holds canvas (1000 x 700), objects (id, kind, x, y, size, color, fill, rotation, flip, z, parts), background, sky, ground, groundColor, mood, selected, last (what the last command made or changed), history (undo snapshots, at most 50) and future (redo)."
    example="Draw a red house."

@art.draw.picture.selected core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which thing is selected?"
    observe=true
    compute=false

files.operations.sop:
@op.art.draw.add core.operation
    impl=add
    semantics=action
    action=draw.add
    doc="Draws one or more things (kind, count, size, color, parts, place) and answers what it drew. Brings the Drawing tab forward."

@op.art.draw.ground core.operation
    impl=ground
    semantics=action
    action=draw.ground
    doc="Adds grass, sand, snow or water to the ground."

@op.art.draw.scene core.operation
    impl=scene
    semantics=action
    action=draw.scene
    doc="Draws a seeded surprise scene with sun, clouds, house, trees and flowers."

@op.art.draw.setMood core.operation
    impl=setMood
    semantics=action
    action=draw.mood
    doc="Night (dark sky, moon and stars), day (blue sky and sun) or sunset."

@op.art.draw.recolor core.operation
    impl=recolor
    semantics=action
    action=draw.recolor
    doc="Colors an object, a part of it (roof, door, wheels), the sky, the ground or the background."

@op.art.draw.givePart core.operation
    impl=givePart
    semantics=action
    action=draw.givePart
    doc="Colors a named part of a thing: give the house a blue door."

@op.art.draw.resize core.operation
    impl=resize
    semantics=action
    action=draw.resize
    doc="Makes things bigger or smaller by a relative amount."

@op.art.draw.matchSize core.operation
    impl=matchSize
    semantics=action
    action=draw.matchSize
    doc="Gives things the same size as another thing: make the tree the same size as the house."

@op.art.draw.setSize core.operation
    impl=setSize
    semantics=action
    action=draw.setSize
    doc="Sets the size by a word: tiny, small, big, huge."

@op.art.draw.move core.operation
    impl=move
    semantics=action
    action=draw.move
    doc="Moves things to a named region, by a step, or next to / above / under / between other things."

@op.art.draw.nudge core.operation
    impl=nudge
    semantics=action
    action=draw.nudge
    doc="Moves things a bit higher, lower, left or right."

@op.art.draw.turn core.operation
    impl=turn
    semantics=action
    action=draw.turn
    doc="Turns things around, to face a side, upside down or by degrees."

@op.art.draw.remove core.operation
    impl=remove
    semantics=action
    action=draw.remove
    doc="Deletes things, the sky color or the ground; \"everything except\" keeps some things."

@op.art.draw.removeIt core.operation
    impl=removeIt
    semantics=action
    action=draw.removeIt
    doc="Deletes the selected thing or what was just drawn (with the editor open: its selection)."

@op.art.draw.clearEverything core.operation
    impl=clearEverything
    semantics=action
    action=draw.clearAll
    doc="Clears the whole picture (shared with the document editor: with the editor open it clears the document)."

@op.art.draw.newDrawing core.operation
    impl=newDrawing
    semantics=action
    action=draw.new
    doc="Starts a new drawing; undo brings the old one back."

@op.art.draw.undo core.operation
    impl=undo
    semantics=action
    action=draw.undo
    doc="Undoes the last change (history of 50); when the editor tab is open it undoes the document instead."

@op.art.draw.redo core.operation
    impl=redo
    semantics=action
    action=draw.redo
    doc="Redoes what was undone."

@op.art.draw.select core.operation
    impl=select
    semantics=action
    action=draw.select
    doc="Selects a thing (outlined in the tab); also what a click on the tab sends."

@op.art.draw.deselect core.operation
    impl=deselect
    semantics=action
    action=draw.deselect
    doc="Clears the selection."

@op.art.draw.fillMode core.operation
    impl=fillMode
    semantics=action
    action=draw.fill
    doc="Fills in with crayon, solid color, or leaves only an outline."

@op.art.draw.duplicate core.operation
    impl=duplicate
    semantics=action
    action=draw.duplicate
    doc="Copies a thing."

@op.art.draw.describe core.operation
    impl=describe
    semantics=action
    action=draw.describe
    doc="Describes the picture in words: things, places, sky and ground."

@op.art.draw.count core.operation
    impl=count
    semantics=action
    action=draw.count
    doc="Counts things of a kind (and color)."

@op.art.draw.whereIs core.operation
    impl=whereIs
    semantics=action
    action=draw.where
    doc="Tells where a thing is."

@op.art.draw.exists core.operation
    impl=exists
    semantics=action
    action=draw.exists
    doc="Tells whether a thing is in the picture."

@op.art.draw.colorOfThing core.operation
    impl=colorOfThing
    semantics=action
    action=draw.colorOf
    doc="Tells the color of a thing, a part, the sky or the ground."

@op.art.draw.whatsNear core.operation
    impl=whatsNear
    semantics=action
    action=draw.near
    doc="Tells what is near a thing."

@op.art.draw.help core.operation
    impl=help
    semantics=action
    action=draw.help
    doc="Tells what can be drawn."

@op.art.draw.colors core.operation
    impl=colors
    semantics=action
    action=draw.colors
    doc="Tells which colors can be used."

@op.art.draw.save core.operation
    impl=save
    semantics=action
    action=draw.save
    doc="Queues the effect draw.download (PNG or SVG)."

@op.art.draw.openTab core.operation
    impl=openTab
    semantics=action
    action=draw.open
    doc="Brings the Drawing tab forward."


@op.art.draw.askKind core.operation
    impl=askKind
    semantics=action
    action=draw.askKind
    doc="Clarification for \"Draw\" without an object: asks what to draw and opens a pending expectation for the missing kind (spec 11)."

@world.common.sense core.world
    namespace=common.sense

    legend=$legend.common.sense
    imports=world.core
    reasoner=matrix
    formalization=rules
    language=en
    status=fixture
    title="Common sense"
    summary=""
    doc="Plain general facts about everyday things and soft rules that use them: where a kind of thing usually is (fish in water, the sun in the sky, trees and houses on the ground), how many there usually are (one sun), and when it is usually not there (no sun at night). It has no patterns, no operations and no host logic, so it is never a routing target. A world uses it by declaration (compose= puts its facts and soft rules in the world's own instance; reads= only the facts), never by copying: the host world tells what it has as common.sense.thing, common.sense.at and common.sense.moment wires and reads the facts for defaults (where a new thing goes). A soft rule never refuses: the host says it as a short friendly warning after doing what was asked. Hand-built platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."

files.mapping.sop:
# How PSys2 legends map onto the library's schema (worker-tasks G2, G8.1).
# Tell this before the legends; the legends are then loaded unchanged.

# A key declaration: the id is <type>.<key>; value= holds literal kinds and $type references.
@psys2.map.key core.schema.map from=core.key
    owner=id.prefix key=id.suffix
    value=value many=card:many required=required ask=ask default=default
    prefix=dynamic          # dynamic=true: any key <key>.<anything> (where.owner, arg.count)

# A type declaration: the id is the type name; a type that names no parent extends core.thing.
@psys2.map.type core.schema.map from=core.type as=type
    name=id extends=extends closed=closed root=core.thing
    complete=closed        # in PSys2 closed=true also means: the world knows every instance
    shared=shared          # the library's shared=true (the facts of the type belong to every namespace): the host adds it to the legend text of the agents (src/reasoner/ns.mjs)

# A legend is a module: namespace= names it, imports= names what it needs.
@psys2.map.legend core.schema.map from=core.legend as=module
    name=namespace imports=imports

    namespace=data.charts
    version=0.1.0
    legend=$legend.data.charts
    imports=world.core
    imports=world.kids.common
    imports=world.kids.arith
    imports=world.kids.shop
    imports=world.kids.tasks
    imports=world.kids.animals
    formalization=rules
    reasoner=matrix
    undo=chart.undo
    redo=chart.redo
    source="the numbers in your charts"
    language=en
    status=fixture
    tab=charts
    tabTitle="Charts"
    tabAlias=chart
    tabAlias=graph
    tabAlias=charts
    tabAlias=graphs
    tabOrder=70
    tabKind=tool
    title="Charts (Chart.js)"
    summary="draw charts"
    doc="Talk with charts drawn by the Chart.js library in the Charts tab: bar, line, pie, doughnut, radar, polar area and scatter. Charts are built from the conversation (what people have, the prices of the toys, a shopping list, the legs of the sea animals) or from numbers you type, and every number of such a chart keeps the ids of the wires it came from. Change the type, title, colors, order, orientation, labels, legend and stacking by language, ask about the data (biggest, total, average, difference, percentage), keep several charts, and download a chart as a picture. State lives in ctx.state; the tab renders it. Hand-built platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."

files.legend.sop:
@legend.diagram.sketch core.legend
    namespace=diagram.sketch
    version=0.1.0
    imports=core
    imports=lang.common
    doc="The diagram: named shapes, connections, groups, facts and rules on an 800 x 500 canvas (cells of 880 x 580 when it grows)"

@diagram.sketch.diagram core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="The diagram. The world state is the source engine's DiagramWorld state: shapes (name, shape, x, y, size, w, h, color, outline, fill, layer, label, font, order), edges (id, from, to, style, arrow, color, label), groups (name, members), rules (shape, size, color, outline), facts, plus last (names the last command made or named), undo / redo (engine snapshots) and rev. The 46 legend questions of the source (imports/diagram-vss-demo/world-draft/legend.json) are the arguments the engine reads from a sentence, not state keys."
    example="Draw a red circle called Start."

Imported platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."

@world.docs.editor core.world
    namespace=docs.editor
    version=0.1.0
    legend=$legend.docs.editor
    imports=world.core
    imports=world.kids.common
    imports=world.kids.tasks
    imports=world.kids.animals
    imports=world.kids.arith
    formalization=rules
    reasoner=matrix
    undo=doc.undo
    redo=doc.redo
    source="the document"
    language=en
    status=fixture
    title="Document editor"
    summary="edit documents"
    doc="A professional document editor you talk to (TipTap in the browser): headings, paragraphs, quotes, bullet, numbered and task lists, tables, lines; formatting by reference (bold, italic, underline, highlight colors, links, size, alignment, conversion); selection and navigation by voice; statistics; undo, read aloud, copy, download as text, markdown or HTML, dictate, and create documents from the conversation (a task list, a report about animals, what people have, a table filled with animals). Every created sentence comes from wires; created blocks keep the source wire ids. State lives in ctx.state, with a TipTap-compatible JSON derived from it. Hand-built platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."

files.operations.sop:
@op.docs.reader.describe core.operation
    impl=describe
    semantics=action
    action=docr.describe
    doc="Introduces the active document: size, sections, main characters, places and key words."

@op.docs.reader.summary core.operation
    impl=summary
    semantics=action
    action=docr.summary
    doc="Extractive summary: the top-scoring sentences (TF-IDF weights), optionally of one section."

@op.docs.reader.characters core.operation
    impl=characters
    semantics=action
    action=docr.characters
    doc="Lists the characters by number of mentions."

@op.docs.reader.mainCharacter core.operation
    impl=mainCharacter
    semantics=action
    action=docr.mainCharacter
    doc="The most mentioned character."

@op.docs.reader.places core.operation
    impl=places
    semantics=action
    action=docr.places
    doc="Places (or things with kind=things) by number of mentions."

@op.docs.reader.keywords core.operation
    impl=keywords
    semantics=action
    action=docr.keywords
    doc="TF-IDF key words."

@op.docs.reader.outline core.operation
    impl=outline
    semantics=action
    action=docr.outline
    doc="Headings of the document with their sentence counts."

@op.docs.reader.stats core.operation
    impl=stats
    semantics=action
    action=docr.stats
    doc="Counts of sentences, words, paragraphs, sections or characters."

@op.docs.reader.who core.operation
    impl=who
    semantics=action
    action=docr.who
    doc="Describes a character, place or thing: roles, relations, attributes, mentions."

@op.docs.reader.did core.operation
    impl=did
    semantics=action
    action=docr.did
    doc="What an entity does: its events (agent - verb - object - place)."

@op.docs.reader.happened core.operation
    impl=happened
    semantics=action
    action=docr.happened
    doc="What happens to an entity: events where it is the object, and how it ends."

@op.docs.reader.where core.operation
    impl=where
    semantics=action
    action=docr.where
    doc="Where an entity lives, goes or is, from event places."

@op.docs.reader.whereDid core.operation
    impl=whereDid
    semantics=action
    action=docr.whereDid
    doc="Where an event happened, found by agent, verb and object words."

@op.docs.reader.whenDid core.operation
    impl=whenDid
    semantics=action
    action=docr.whenDid

@op.docs.reader.didV core.operation
    impl=didV
    semantics=action
    action=docr.didV

@op.docs.reader.said core.operation
    impl=said
    semantics=action
    action=docr.said

@op.docs.reader.saying core.operation
    impl=saying
    semantics=action
    action=docr.saying
    doc="What an entity says."

@op.docs.reader.part core.operation
    impl=part
    semantics=action
    action=docr.part

@op.docs.reader.sentence core.operation
    impl=sentence

@op.docs.reader.count core.operation

    semantics=action

files.patterns.sop:
@pat.docs.reader.describe core.pattern
    match="[can_you|could_you]? [describe|introduce|analyse|analyze|profile|inspect] [the|this|that|my]? {d:lex.docs.reader.docs}"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.describe"
    kind=request
    priority=15
    example="Describe the story."
    example="Analyze the file."

@pat.docs.reader.describe.know core.pattern
    match="what do you know about [the|this|that|my] {d:lex.docs.reader.docs}"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.describe"
    kind=question
    priority=15
    example="What do you know about the file?"

@pat.docs.reader.summary.about core.pattern
    canonical="What is the story about?"
    match="what is [the|this|that|my] {d:lex.docs.reader.docs} [all_about|about]"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.summary"
    kind=question
    priority=15
    example="What is the story about?"

@pat.docs.reader.summary.k core.pattern
    match="[can_you|could_you]? [summarize|summarise|recap] [the|this|that|my]? {d:lex.docs.reader.docs?} in {k:number} [sentences|sentence]"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.summary arg.k={k}"
    kind=request
    priority=12
    example="Summarize the story in 3 sentences."

@pat.docs.reader.summary.give core.pattern
    match="[can_you|could_you]? [give_me|show_me|tell_me|write] [a|the]? [short|brief|quick]? [summary|recap|gist|synopsis] [of]? [the|this|that|my]? {d:lex.docs.reader.docs?}"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.summary"
    kind=request
    priority=12
    example="Give me a short summary of the story."

@pat.docs.reader.summary.sec.about core.pattern
    match="what is [section|chapter] {n:number} about"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.summary arg.n={n}"
    kind=question
    priority=12
    example="What is section 3 about?"

@pat.docs.reader.summary.sec.about.ord core.pattern
    match="what is the {o:lex.docs.reader.ordinals} [section|chapter] about"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.summary arg.ord={o}"
    kind=question
    priority=12
    example="What is the first section about?"

@pat.docs.reader.characters core.pattern
    match="who are [all]? [the]? [main|important|key]? [characters|people|persons] [in|of]? [the|this]? {d:lex.docs.reader.docs?}"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=docr.characters"
    kind=question
    priority=12

files.samples/hansel-and-gretel.md:
# Hansel and Gretel

> Source: a short English retelling of the fairy tale collected by the Brothers Grimm (Kinder- und Hausmärchen, 1812). The tale is in the public domain; this retelling was written for this project and is released under CC0 (public domain dedication).

## The Poor Woodcutter

Once upon a time a poor woodcutter lived at the edge of a great forest with his two children and their stepmother. The boy was called Hansel and his little sister was called Gretel. The woodcutter was their father. He loved his children, but the family had almost nothing to eat. The stepmother was cruel and she hated the children.

One evening the stepmother spoke to the father. "There is not enough bread for four," she said. "Tomorrow you must take the children deep into the forest and leave them there." The father wept, but he agreed in the end. Hansel heard every word through the thin wall of the bedroom. He told his sister about the plan. "Do not cry, Gretel," he whispered. "I will find a way."

Hansel crept out of the house at night and filled his pockets with white pebbles. In the morning the father led the children into the forest. Hansel dropped a pebble on the path every few steps. The father lit a fire and went away. The children waited until the moon rose. The white pebbles shone in the moonlight and showed them the way home. The father was glad to see them, but the stepmother was furious.

## Lost in the Forest

A few days later the stepmother made the father take the children into the forest again. This time Hansel had no pebbles, so he scattered crumbs of bread on the path. The birds ate every crumb. When night came, Hansel and Gretel were lost. They walked for three days and grew hungry and tired.

At last they saw a white bird. It led them to a little house in a clearing. The walls of the house were made of bread and the roof was made of cake. The windows were made of clear sugar. Hansel ate a piece of the roof and Gretel ate a piece of the window. "Nibble, nibble, little mouse, who is nibbling at my house?" called a voice from inside.

The door opened and an old woman came out. She was a witch, but she smiled kindly at the children. "Come in, dear children," said the witch. "You will have food and a warm bed." Hansel and Gretel followed her into the house. They did not know that the witch built her house of bread to catch hungry children.

## The Witch's Oven

Early the next morning the witch locked Hansel in a small cage. She made Gretel carry water and cook for her brother. "Fatten him up," said the witch. "I will eat him when he is fat." Every day the witch came to the cage and said, "Hansel, put out your finger so that I can feel how fat you are." Hansel held out a thin bone instead of his finger. The witch could not see well, so she thought the bone was his finger. She was angry that Hansel stayed so thin.

After four weeks the witch lost her patience. "Gretel, climb into the oven and see if it is hot enough," she ordered. Gretel guessed the witch's plan. "I do not know how," said Gretel. "Show me first." The witch bent over and put her head into the oven. Gretel pushed her with all her strength and shut the iron door. The witch burned in her own oven.

Gretel ran to the cage and set her brother free. "The witch is dead!" she cried. Hansel and Gretel hugged each other and danced with joy. They found pearls and jewels in every corner of the witch's house. They filled their pockets and their aprons and set off for home.

## Home Again

On their way they came to a wide lake. A white duck carried Hansel and Gretel across the water, one after the other. Soon they saw the woodcutter's house through the trees. They ran inside and threw their arms around their father. The father had not had a happy hour since he lost the children. The stepmother was dead. Gretel shook out her apron and the pearls rolled over the floor. From that day on the family lived together without worry, and the father was never poor again.

@op.games.chess.why core.operation
    impl=matrix
    semantics=action
    action=chess.why
    doc="Matrix mode: why the computer played its last move (it mates, castles, promotes, captures, gives check, develops a piece, takes the center, or was the best move found), from what the move did, recorded on its wire."

@pat.games.chess.m.why core.pattern
    match="[$lang.lead.filler|pls|hey]? why [$lang.why.did] you [$lang.why.act] [$lang.why.there]"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=chess.why"
    kind=request
    priority=14
    example="Why did you play that?"
    canonical="Why did you play that?"
    example="Why did you move that piece?"

@pat.games.chess.m.why.short core.pattern
    match="[$lang.lead.filler|pls|hey]? why [$lang.why.place]"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=chess.why"
    kind=request
    priority=14
    example="Why that move?"
files.matrix.templates.sop:
@tpl.games.chess.m.why core.template
    for=action.chess.why
    text="{value}"

    for=action.chess.why

    text="I have not played yet."

files.data/README.md:
# Data of the world geo.map

All files here and the knowledge base (`kb.sop`) and place lexicon (`lexicon.sop`) are generated by `scripts/build-geo-data.mjs` from npm packages. Do not edit them by hand.

| Data | Package (version) | Licence | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Countries: names, capitals, region, borders, area, currencies, languages, landlocked | world-countries 5.1.0 (mledoze/countries) | ODbL 1.0 (attribution and share-alike for the database) | `geo.map.country` wires |
| Country population | country-json 2.3.0 (country-by-population, about 2018 estimates) | MIT | `pop` of countries (Timor-Leste added by hand: World Bank 2018) |
| Cities | all-the-cities 3.1.0 (GeoNames gazetteer, https://www.geonames.org) | CC BY 4.0 (attribution required) | `geo.map.city` wires: 246 capitals, every city of 500,000+ people, Romanian and Moldovan cities of 30,000+ (1001 in all) |
| Country outlines (offline base map) | world-atlas 2.0.2 countries-50m (Natural Earth) | public domain | `docs/webchat/vendor/map/countries-50m.json`, bounding boxes of countries (`bb`) |
| Groups (EU, NATO, Nordic ...) | hand-written, as of 2024 | none | `geo.map.region` wires of kind `group` |

Every KB wire carries its source and licence in `core.source`. Population figures are rough and dated; city populations are GeoNames city-proper values (a few large cities are much smaller than their metro areas).

Counts: 250 countries and territories (194 independent), 1001 cities, 38 regions, 1464 lexicon names. Capitals without a GeoNames match (no city wire; the capital name is still known): EH:El Aaiún, IO:Diego Garcia, TK:Fakaofo.

Rebuild: `npm i world-countries@5.1.0 all-the-cities@3.1.0 country-json@2.3.0 world-atlas@2.0.2 topojson-client@3.1.0` in a temporary directory, then `node scripts/build-geo-data.mjs --modules <dir>/node_modules`.

files.matrix.sop:
# kids.animals as a matrix: the animals are wires (the knowledge base kb.sop, and what the dialogue teaches or tells about pets), and a question about one is
# a query the library answers by itself: the class, the legs, the food, the sound, the baby's name, the pets, and the abilities (can_fly and can_swim: an
# explicit "no" is kept apart from unknown, "yes" and "no" together are a conflict, and the library says which statements it rests on). There are no rules of
# our own to add: nothing follows from the facts that a child has not said (an animal is not guessed to fly from its class).
#
# Left to the operations (ops.mjs, `ops=` in world.sop): the checks that carry the value they seek ("is a whale a fish?": the library supposes a wire with the
# value it was given and answers it), the phrases of where an animal lives and what covers it (several habitats are one sentence), the description of an animal
# and the search for the animals that match several properties. Why the library does not do the habitats and coverings (searched in the library's docs and
# source, 2026-11-11): several values of a key are a `conflicting` answer in value mode, and `mode=list` is the only way to get them as `supported`; the
# question wires of kids.animals' patterns are shared with the ops strategy and carry no mode, and a template without `mode` renders value questions only. A key
# cannot say "answer as a list" (there is no `answer=list` or `combine=union` for a query), and no aggregate joins the values into one text (`collect` makes
# several values again). The issue is written in worker-log.md. Conflicting taught facts need nothing more: the library says them (a conflict, not a refusal).
# Their words are the world's own tables in ops.mjs.

# What a child teaches is told as wires and is undone with the rest (undo, "that's wrong"); `fns.mjs` says in the world's words what was taken back.
files.matrix.templates.sop:
@tpl.kids.animals.m.can_fly.yes core.template
    for=kids.animals.animal.can_fly
    when="value=true"
    text="Yes, {name:a} can fly."

@tpl.kids.animals.m.can_fly.no core.template
    for=kids.animals.animal.can_fly
    when="value=false"

files.legend.sop:
@legend.kids.arith core.legend
    namespace=kids.arith
    version=0.1.0
    imports=core
    imports=kids.common
    doc="Counting things people have, events that change the counts, totals, comparisons and bare arithmetic"

@kids.arith.holding core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Someone has a number of items of one kind. A statement sets the count; later events change it."
    example="Tom has 5 apples."
    negative="Tom likes apples."

@kids.arith.holding.owner core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who has them?"

@kids.arith.holding.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.holding.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many are there?"
    observe=true
    compute=true

@kids.arith.holding.start core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many were there at the start?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.change core.type
    extends=core.event
    doc="Something happens to the number of items someone has. Events are applied in dialog order (core.seq)."
    example="Ana gives Tom 3 apples."

@kids.arith.change.who core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is it about (who gives, gets, eats, loses, buys or breaks)?"

@kids.arith.change.to core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who receives the items?"

@kids.arith.change.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.change.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many items are involved?"

@kids.arith.give core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="One person gives some items to another person: who gives, to receives."
    example="Ana gives Tom 3 apples."

@kids.arith.receive core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone gets, receives or finds some items."
    example="Tom finds 2 marbles."

@kids.arith.eat core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone eats some items."
    example="Tom ate 2 apples."

@kids.arith.lose core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone loses some items."
    example="Mia lost 3 marbles."

@kids.arith.buy core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone buys some items (only the counts are tracked here, not the money)."
    example="Ben buys 4 pencils."

@kids.arith.break core.type
    extends=kids.arith.change
    doc="Someone breaks some items."
    example="Sam broke 2 pencils."

@kids.arith.total core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="How many items of one kind there are altogether, over everybody or over two named people."
    example="How many apples are there altogether?"

@kids.arith.total.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.total.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person to count?"

@kids.arith.total.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person to count?"

@kids.arith.total.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many are there altogether?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.leader core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Who has the most items of one kind, or who of two named people has more."
    example="Who has more apples, Tom or Ana?"

@kids.arith.leader.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.leader.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person to compare?"

@kids.arith.leader.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person to compare?"

@kids.arith.leader.winner core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who has more?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.gap core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="How many more (or fewer) items of one kind the first person has than the second."
    example="How many more apples does Tom have than Ana?"

@kids.arith.gap.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.gap.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person?"

@kids.arith.gap.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person?"

@kids.arith.gap.diff core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the difference between the two counts?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.verdict core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Yes or no: does the first person have more items than the second?"
    example="Does Tom have more apples than Ana?"

@kids.arith.verdict.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.verdict.who1 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the first person?"

@kids.arith.verdict.who2 core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who is the second person?"

@kids.arith.verdict.answer core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Is it yes or no?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.has core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Yes or no: does someone have any items of one kind?"
    example="Does Tom have any apples?"

@kids.arith.has.owner core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who might have them?"

@kids.arith.has.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.has.answer core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Is it yes or no?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.calc core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A bare calculation of two numbers: plus, minus, times, divided_by."
    example="What is 7 plus 5?"

@kids.arith.calc.op core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which operation (plus, minus, times, divided_by)?"

@kids.arith.calc.a core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the first number?"

@kids.arith.calc.b core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the second number?"

@kids.arith.calc.result core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the result?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.half core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Half of a number."
    example="What is half of 10?"

@kids.arith.half.n core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="Which number?"

@kids.arith.half.result core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is half of it?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.double core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Double a number."
    example="What is double 6?"

@kids.arith.double.n core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="Which number?"

@kids.arith.double.result core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is double it?"
    compute=true

@kids.arith.calc.op2 core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which second operation (plus, minus, times, divided_by)?"

@kids.arith.calc.c core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="What is the third number?"

@kids.arith.relation core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="One person has some more, some fewer, or some times as many items of one kind as another: a comparison told as a statement. It fixes the count of whichever of the two is not known yet, from the one that is."
    example="Ana has 3 more apples than Ion."
    negative="Ana has more apples."

@kids.arith.relation.who core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who has more, fewer or times as many?"

@kids.arith.relation.ref core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Compared with whom?"

@kids.arith.relation.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.relation.kind core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="More, fewer or times as many?"

@kids.arith.relation.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many more, fewer or times as many?"

@kids.arith.negated core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="Someone did not do something to the counts (did not give, eat, lose, buy, break or get any). It is understood and said back, and nothing changes: the counts are not touched."
    example="Ana does not give Ion any apples."
    negative="Ana gives Ion 3 apples."

@kids.arith.negated.who core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who did not do it?"

@kids.arith.negated.to core.key
    value=$core.agent
    card=one
    ask="Who would have received the items?"

@kids.arith.negated.verb core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What did not happen (give, eat, lose, buy, break, get)?"

@kids.arith.negated.item core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="What kind of thing is it?"

@kids.arith.negated.count core.key
    value=number
    card=one
    ask="How many (when a number was said)?"

files.operations.sop:
@op.kids.arith.currentCount core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.holding.count
    inputs=kids.arith.holding.owner
    inputs=kids.arith.holding.item
    impl=currentCount
    semantics=query
    doc="The number someone has after applying, in dialog order, every statement of having and every giving, getting, eating, losing, buying and breaking. A person whose starting count is unknown stays unknown; an impossible event gives a conflict."

@op.kids.arith.startCount core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.holding.start
    inputs=kids.arith.holding.owner
    inputs=kids.arith.holding.item
    impl=startCount
    semantics=query
    doc="How many someone had at the start: the first number said, or worked out from an event and the result afterwards (ate 2 and now has 3: 5)."

@op.kids.arith.totalCount core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.total.count
    inputs=kids.arith.total.item
    inputs=kids.arith.total.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.total.who2
    impl=totalCount
    semantics=query
    doc="The sum of the counts of everybody whose count is known (or of two named people)."

@op.kids.arith.leader core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.leader.winner
    inputs=kids.arith.leader.item
    inputs=kids.arith.leader.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.leader.who2
    impl=leader
    semantics=query
    doc="Who has the most (or more, between two people). A tie is ambiguous."

@op.kids.arith.gap core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.gap.diff
    inputs=kids.arith.gap.item
    inputs=kids.arith.gap.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.gap.who2
    impl=gap
    semantics=query
    doc="How many more or fewer items the first person has than the second."

@op.kids.arith.verdict core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.verdict.answer
    inputs=kids.arith.verdict.item
    inputs=kids.arith.verdict.who1
    inputs=kids.arith.verdict.who2
    impl=verdict
    semantics=query
    doc="Yes or no: does the first person have more than the second?"

@op.kids.arith.hasAny core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.has.answer
    inputs=kids.arith.has.owner
    inputs=kids.arith.has.item
    impl=hasAny
    semantics=query
    doc="Yes or no: does the person have at least one item of the kind?"

@op.kids.arith.calc core.operation
    outputs=kids.arith.calc.result

files.patterns.sop:
@pat.kids.arith.has core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [now]? [has|have|had] [got|now]? {n:number} {item:lex.kids.arith.items} [now|left|today|at_first|at_the_start]?"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={n} item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=9
    example="Tom has 5 apples."

@pat.kids.arith.has.a core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [now]? [has|have|had] [got]? [a|an] {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count=1 item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=10
    example="Mia has a pear."

@pat.kids.arith.has.no core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [has|have|had] [got]? no {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count=0 item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=10
    example="Ben has no marbles."

@pat.kids.arith.has.start core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [starts|started|begins|began] with {n:number} {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={n} item={item}"
    kind=statement
    priority=10
    example="Lily starts with 8 stickers."

@pat.kids.arith.has.two core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [has|have|had] [got]? {n:number} {item:lex.kids.arith.items} and {m:number} {item2:lex.kids.arith.items}"
    emit="@{_} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={n} item={item}\n@{_1} kids.arith.holding owner={who} count={m} item={item2}"
    kind=statement
    priority=11
    example="Tom has 4 apples and 3 pears."

@pat.kids.arith.give.direct core.pattern
    match="{who:agent} [gives|gave|give] {to:agent} {n:number} [more]? {item:lex.kids.arith.items}"

    priority=9
    example="Ana gives Tom 3 apples."

    kind=statement
    priority=10

files.matrix.patterns.sop:
@pat.kids.tasks.m.add.bare core.pattern
    match="[$lang.lead.polite|pls|hey|just|so]? [$kids.tasks.g46_add] [to|on|onto|into|in] [my|the|our|a] list [$lang.tail.filler]?"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=tasks.add arg.list=to-do"
    kind=request
    priority=12

files.operations.sop:
@op.kids.tasks.add core.operation
    impl=addItems
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.add
    doc="Adds one or more items (split at commas and \"and\") to a list; items already there are reported, not added twice."

@op.kids.tasks.remind core.operation
    impl=remindMe
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.remind
    doc="Adds an item to the reminders list (no real timer)."

@op.kids.tasks.remove core.operation
    impl=removeItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.remove
    doc="Removes items from one list or from whichever list has them; says when an item is not there."

@op.kids.tasks.done core.operation
    impl=finishItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.done
    doc="Marks an item as done; asks which one when several match; says when it is already done."

@op.kids.tasks.notDone core.operation
    impl=notDone
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.notDone
    doc="The user says they did NOT do something (I didn't buy milk): nothing is ticked off, the answer says so and offers to tick it off later."

@op.kids.tasks.check core.operation
    impl=checkItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.check
    doc="Tells whether an item is done (yes) or still to do or unknown (missing)."

@op.kids.tasks.show core.operation
    impl=showList
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.show
    doc="Lists the items still to do on a list and the items that are done."

@op.kids.tasks.pending core.operation
    impl=pendingItems
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.pending
    doc="Lists the items of a list that are not done yet."

@op.kids.tasks.count core.operation
    impl=countItems
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.count
    doc="Counts the items on a list."

@op.kids.tasks.countPending core.operation
    impl=countPending
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.countPending
    doc="Counts the items of a list that are not done yet."

@op.kids.tasks.has core.operation
    impl=hasItem
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.has
    doc="Tells whether an item is on a list."

@op.kids.tasks.clear core.operation
    impl=clearList
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.clear
    doc="Removes every item of a list."

@op.kids.tasks.lists core.operation
    impl=showLists
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.lists
    doc="Lists the lists that have items, with their sizes."

@op.kids.tasks.whichList core.operation
    impl=whichList
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.whichList
    doc="Which list the last item was put on, and whether the list was an assumption (the user did not name it)."

@op.kids.tasks.whyDone core.operation
    impl=whyDone
    semantics=action
    action=tasks.whyDone
    doc="Why an item is done: the user marked it done."

    card=one

@op.kids.time.monthDays core.operation
    outputs=kids.time.monthinfo.days
    inputs=kids.time.monthinfo.name
    impl=monthDays
    semantics=query
    doc="The number of days of a month from the calendar knowledge, with a note for February."

@op.kids.time.shift core.operation
    outputs=kids.time.shift.result
    inputs=kids.time.shift.unit
    inputs=kids.time.shift.from
    inputs=kids.time.shift.by
    impl=shift
    semantics=query
    doc="The day, month or season some steps after or before another one, wrapping around; today and this month come from the dialog."

@op.kids.time.daysBetween core.operation
    outputs=kids.time.gap.count
    inputs=kids.time.gap.from
    inputs=kids.time.gap.to
    impl=daysBetween
    semantics=query
    doc="How many days until a day of the week comes, counting forward."

@op.kids.time.hoursBetween core.operation
    outputs=kids.time.hoursgap.count
    inputs=kids.time.hoursgap.from
    inputs=kids.time.hoursgap.to
    impl=hoursBetween
    semantics=compute
    doc="How many hours from one o'clock to another on a 12-hour clock."

@op.kids.time.length core.operation
    outputs=kids.time.length.count
    inputs=kids.time.length.whole
    inputs=kids.time.length.part

    doc="How many smaller spans fit in a bigger one: a fact from the knowledge base or a product along a chain of facts."

    impl=shift
    semantics=query
    doc="The season some steps after or before another one, wrapping around."

files.operations.sop:
@op.ui.avatar.setPart core.operation
    impl=setPart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setPart
    doc="Sets a component by name and by synonym (visor eyes, a dish on top, a medical mask). When only another character has it, the avatar becomes that character. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setPartUnknown core.operation
    impl=setPartUnknown
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setPartUnknown
    doc="A component named with words that are not a known variant: says what is possible. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.step core.operation
    impl=step
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.step
    doc="Next, previous or different variant of a component (dir=next|previous|different). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.resizePart core.operation
    impl=resizePart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.resizePart
    doc="Bigger or smaller (dir=bigger|smaller) for a part. Emoji eyes step along the sizes that really differ (small, pupils, big pupils); the robot and the person cannot scale their eyes, so the answer offers the styles that look bigger or smaller. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.nameOf core.operation
    impl=nameOf
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.nameOf
    doc="The bare name of the avatar. kids.common speaks it as the assistant's name (the avatar and the assistant are one character): ctx.request(\"avatar.nameOf\"). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.resetPart core.operation
    impl=resetPart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.resetPart
    doc="Back to the default variant of one component. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.removePart core.operation
    impl=removePart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.removePart
    doc="Takes off a component that can be absent (mask, glasses, antenna) or a hat. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.removeAll core.operation
    impl=removeAll
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.removeAll
    doc="Takes off everything that can be taken off. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setColor core.operation
    impl=setColor
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setColor
    doc="Sets a color part to the nearest entry of the style palette for a named color. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.shiftColor core.operation
    impl=shiftColor
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.shiftColor
    doc="Makes a color part lighter or darker, one palette step. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askColor core.operation
    impl=askColor
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askColor
    doc="Tells the color of a part in words. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.listColors core.operation
    impl=listColors
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.listColors
    doc="Lists the colors a part can have, or the colored parts of the character. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.surprise core.operation
    impl=surprise
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.surprise
    doc="Random look from a new recorded seed (mode=surprise) or everything different (mode=everything). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setSeed core.operation
    impl=setSeed
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setSeed
    doc="Draws the character from a given seed; the same seed always gives the same look. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askSeed core.operation
    impl=askSeed
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askSeed
    doc="Tells the seed. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setCharacter core.operation
    impl=setCharacter
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setCharacter
    doc="Becomes one of the characters (robot, person, emoji, portrait, cartoon, kid, pixel person, pixel robot, fun emoji), or a woman, man, girl, boy, old or little one with a fitting style and hair preset (kind=), optionally with a mood and with or without glasses or a beard. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.pickCharacter core.operation
    impl=pickCharacter
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.pickCharacter
    doc="Picks a character of the gallery by its number (the third one) or steps through the gallery (next, previous character). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askCharacter core.operation
    impl=askCharacter
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askCharacter
    doc="Tells which character is shown. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.listCharacters core.operation
    impl=listCharacters
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.listCharacters
    doc="Lists the characters. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setMood core.operation
    impl=setMood
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setMood
    doc="Sets an expression by mood word, mapped per character. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.checkMood core.operation
    impl=checkMood
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.checkMood
    doc="Yes or no: do I look like that? Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askMood core.operation
    impl=askMood
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askMood
    doc="Tells the mood the expression stands for. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setName core.operation
    impl=setName
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setName
    doc="Gives the avatar a name. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askName core.operation
    impl=askName
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askName
    doc="Tells the name. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.reset core.operation
    impl=reset
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.reset
    doc="Back to the default look (scope=all: all characters, and the robot). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.animate core.operation
    impl=animate
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.animate
    doc="Queues the effect avatar.animate (wave, nod, dance, wink ...): a moment, not stored state. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askParts core.operation
    impl=askParts
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askParts
    doc="Tells what can be changed. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.listOptions core.operation
    impl=listOptions
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.listOptions
    doc="Lists the variants of a component in words. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askPart core.operation
    impl=askPart
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askPart
    doc="Tells what the avatar has for a component. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.hasThing core.operation
    impl=hasThing
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.hasThing
    doc="Yes or no: does the avatar have or wear something? Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.askWearing core.operation
    impl=askWearing
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.askWearing
    doc="Tells what the avatar wears. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.describe core.operation
    impl=describe
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.describe
    doc="Describes the whole avatar in words. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.undo core.operation
    impl=undo
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.undo
    doc="Goes back to the look before the last change (also a change of character). Keeps up to 20 steps in the state. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.explainSwitch core.operation
    impl=explainSwitch
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.explainSwitch
    doc="Apologises and explains a change of character, and says how to go back. Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."

@op.ui.avatar.setPartColored core.operation
    impl=setPartColored
    semantics=action
    action=avatar.setPartColored
    doc="Sets a component and colors it when the character can color it (a red hat). Every changing command also brings the avatar tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\")."
files.patterns.sop:
@pat.ui.avatar.setpart core.pattern
    match="[$lang.lead.filler|pls|plz]? [$lang.lead.polite]? [$ui.avatar.g7_give_yourself] [a|an|the|your|some|new|ur]? {v:lex.ui.avatar.options} {n:number?} [$ui.avatar.g12_on]? {p:lex.ui.avatar.parts?} [$lang.tail.filler]?"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=avatar.setPart arg.part={p} arg.value={v} arg.n={n} arg.text=\"{v}\""
    kind=request
    priority=12
    example="Give yourself visor eyes."
    example="Use the cyclops eye."
    example="Wear a medical mask."
    example="Put on glasses."
    example="Give yourself glasses 3."
    example="Wear sunglasses."
    example="I want a dish on top."
    example="Try a heart on your chest."

@pat.ui.avatar.setpart.after core.pattern
    match="[$lang.lead.filler|pls|plz]? [$lang.lead.polite]? [$ui.avatar.g7_give_yourself] [a|an|the|your|some|new|ur]? {v:lex.ui.avatar.options} [on|on_your|on_my|on_the|in|in_your|for_your]? {p:lex.ui.avatar.parts} {n:number} [$lang.tail.filler]?"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=avatar.setPart arg.part={p} arg.value={v} arg.n={n} arg.text=\"{v}\""
    kind=request
    priority=12
    example="Give yourself short curly hair."
    example="Give yourself a moustache 4."

@pat.ui.avatar.resize.grow core.pattern
    match="[$lang.lead.filler|pls|plz]? [$lang.lead.polite]? [enlarge|widen|grow|expand|enlarge_your|widen_your|increase|upsize|make_larger|make_bigger] [your|the|ur]? {p:lex.ui.avatar.parts} [$lang.tail.filler]?"
    emit="@{_} core.request action=avatar.resizePart arg.part={p} arg.dir=bigger"
    kind=request
    priority=13
    example="Enlarge your eyes."
    example="Increase the eyes."

@pat.ui.avatar.resize.shrink core.pattern

files.matrix.sop:
# ui.help as a matrix: what each area of the app can do is the knowledge base (kb.sop, generated by scripts/gen-ui-kb.mjs from the manifests and the canonical examples
# of the patterns), and "what can you do in the map?" is a question the library answers by looking the area up. There is very little state, and the library adds
# little to this world: the choice of the examples to show (a rotation over a world's patterns, the closest examples to a sentence, edit distance) stays in ops.mjs.
#   ui.help.state   one, once the help was used: rest = the state ops.mjs keeps as JSON (the rotation cursor of each world, the last help, the last sentence that was not
#                   understood). The world is passive: the dialog layer writes `lastUnparsed` after a failed sentence and that is not a step of the turn; only a help
#                   request is, so "undo that" after "more examples" puts the rotation back.

@hp.seq core.sequence key=core.seq

@hp.k.rest core.slot of=ui.help.state key=rest kind=blob required=true

    impl=capabilities
    semantics=action
    action=chat.capabilities
    doc="A short spoken answer built from the summary= phrase of every loaded world (the title when a world has none), grouped by leading verb (uses ctx.worlds())."

@op.ui.help.help core.operation

    action=ui.help
    doc="Five varied example commands for the active tab, from the pattern examples of the world that owns the tab (ctx.patterns); repeating the request, or asking for more, gives the next five. With arg.count=1 gives a single example."

files.operations.sop:
@op.ui.shell.openTab core.operation
    impl=openTab
    semantics=action
    action=ui.openTab
    doc="Makes a tab the active tab (remembers the previous one). Also the documented cross-world request other tool worlds use to bring their tab forward: ctx.request(\"ui.openTab\", { tab })."

@op.ui.shell.playGame core.operation
    impl=playGame
    semantics=action
    action=ui.playGame
    doc="Opens a game tab and starts a game there through the game world (ctx.request)."

@op.ui.shell.chooseGame core.operation
    impl=chooseGame
    semantics=action
    action=ui.chooseGame
    doc="Lists the games that can be played."

@op.ui.shell.back core.operation
    impl=back
    semantics=action
    action=ui.back
    doc="Returns to the previous tab."

@op.ui.shell.whichTab core.operation
    impl=whichTab
    semantics=action
    action=ui.whichTab
    doc="Says which tab is open."

@op.ui.shell.speaker core.operation
    impl=speaker
    semantics=action
    action=ui.speaker
    doc="Turns the speaker on or off (effect speech.cancel when turned off)."

@op.ui.shell.listening core.operation
    impl=listening
    semantics=action
    action=ui.listening
    doc="Turns the microphone listening on or off."

@op.ui.shell.handsFree core.operation
    impl=handsFree
    semantics=action
    action=ui.handsFree
    doc="Turns hands-free mode on (which also starts listening) or off (which also stops listening)."

@op.ui.shell.rate core.operation
    impl=rate
    semantics=action
    action=ui.rate
    doc="Makes the speech slower or faster by 0.25 (range 0.5 to 2) or sets it to a value."

@op.ui.shell.language core.operation
    impl=language
    semantics=action
    action=ui.language
    doc="Sets the interface, recognition and speech language (en or ro)."

@op.ui.shell.newGame core.operation
    impl=newGame
    semantics=action
    action=ui.newGame
    doc="Starts a new game in the game of the active tab (ctx.request)."

@op.ui.shell.giveUp core.operation
    impl=giveUp
    semantics=action
    action=ui.giveUp
    doc="Gives up the game of the active tab (ctx.request)."

@op.ui.shell.hint core.operation
    impl=hint
    semantics=action
    action=ui.hint
    doc="Asks the game of the active tab for a hint (ctx.request)."

@op.ui.shell.phraseLog core.operation
    impl=phraseLog
    semantics=action
    action=ui.phraseLog
    doc="Phrase log of the host (what the user typed or said, kept in the browser): shows it in Settings, exports it, or reports its size. Effect phraselog { what: show | export | count } is carried out by the host."

@op.ui.shell.settings core.operation
    impl=settings
    semantics=action
    action=ui.settings
    doc="Opens the host's Settings dialog (optionally on one tab: understanding, language, voice, phrases, models, developer, about) or closes it. Effect settings { action: open | close, tab } is carried out by the host."

files.legend.sop:
@legend.user.profile core.legend
    namespace=user.profile
    version=0.1.0
    imports=core
    imports=kids.common
    doc="A profile of the user, built in a game-like conversation: the plan (sections and fields with priority, sensitivity and questions) and what is known. The keys of user.profile.person are the profile fields; their ask is the canonical question."

@user.profile.person core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="The user. Each key is a profile field; values are kept in the world state with their provenance (said or guessed)."
    example="I am a nurse."

@user.profile.person.name core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What should I call you?"

@user.profile.person.address core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="How should I address you?"

@user.profile.person.location core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Where are you based?"

@user.profile.person.role core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is your current role?"

@user.profile.person.field core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Which field or industry do you work in?"

@user.profile.person.org core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Which organisation do you work for?"

@user.profile.person.years core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="How many years of experience do you have?"

@user.profile.person.previous core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="What did you do before?"

@user.profile.person.education core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is your educational background?"

@user.profile.person.skills core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="What are your main skills?"

@user.profile.person.tools core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="Which tools or languages do you use?"

@user.profile.person.hobbies core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="What are your hobbies?"

@user.profile.person.topics core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="Which topics interest you?"

@user.profile.person.media core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="Which books, music or films do you like?"

@user.profile.person.sports core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="Which sports do you like?"

@user.profile.person.learning core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="What would you like to learn?"

@user.profile.person.career core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What are your career goals?"

@user.profile.person.year core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is your goal for this year?"

@user.profile.person.length core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Do you prefer short or detailed answers?"

@user.profile.person.tone core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Do you prefer a formal or a casual tone?"

@user.profile.person.language core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="Which language do you prefer?"

@user.profile.section core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A section of the profile (the sections of the CV card)."
    example="Professional"

@user.profile.section.label core.key
    value=string
    ask="What is the section called?"

@user.profile.section.order core.key
    value=integer
    ask="Where does the section come in the CV?"

@user.profile.field core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A planned profile field: where it belongs, how important it is, how sensitive, and how to ask for it."
    example="Current role"

@user.profile.field.label core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is the field called?"

@user.profile.field.section core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which section does the field belong to?"

@user.profile.field.prio core.key
    value=integer
    card=one
    ask="How important is it to learn (1 to 10)?"

@user.profile.field.card core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Is there one value (one) or several (many)?"

@user.profile.field.sens core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="How sensitive is it (none, low, medium, high)?"

@user.profile.field.want core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What would we like to learn, in words?"

@user.profile.field.example core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is an example answer?"

@user.profile.field.q core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="How can the question be phrased?"

@user.profile.field.follow core.key
    value=string
    card=one
    ask="What is the follow-up question?"

@user.profile.field.followKey core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which field does the answer to the follow-up fill (empty: it is kept as a note)?"

@user.profile.field.followMode core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="When is the follow-up asked (always or unclear answers only)?"

@user.profile.field.ack core.key
    value=string
    card=many
    ask="How can the system acknowledge an answer ({v} the value, {V} capitalised, {A} with a or an)?"

@user.profile.field.needs core.key
    value=atom
    card=one
    ask="Which field must be known before this one is asked?"

@user.profile.field.askable core.key
    value=boolean
    card=one
    ask="May the system ask for it?"

@user.profile.industry core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A field or industry, with the words that name it."
    example="Healthcare"

@user.profile.industry.label core.key
    value=string
    ask="What is the field called?"

@user.profile.industry.word core.key
    value=atom
    card=many
    ask="Which words name the field?"

@user.profile.reaction core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="A short warm reaction to a specific answer."
    example="A nurse: that takes stamina!"

@user.profile.reaction.kind core.key
    value=atom
    ask="What kind of answer does it react to (role, hobby, field)?"

@user.profile.reaction.word core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which answer (lexicon form) does it react to?"

@user.profile.reaction.text core.key
    value=string
    ask="What does the system say?"

@user.profile.activity core.type
    extends=core.state
    doc="An activity word that implies a role (teaching implies teacher)."
    example="I have been teaching for 12 years."

@user.profile.activity.word core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which activity word?"

@user.profile.activity.role core.key
    value=atom
    ask="Which role does it imply?"

files.world.sop:
@world.user.profile core.world
    namespace=user.profile
    version=0.1.0
    legend=$legend.user.profile
    imports=world.core
    imports=world.kids.common
    formalization=rules
    reasoner=matrix
    source="what you told me about yourself"
    language=en
    status=fixture
    tab=profile
    tabTitle="Profile"
    tabAlias=profile
    tabAlias=my_profile
    tabAlias=about_me
    tabAlias=cv
    tabAlias=resume
    tabAlias=my_cv
    tabOrder=90
    tabKind=tool
    title="User profile"
    summary="get to know you and keep your profile"
    doc="Gets to know the user through a short, game-like interview (one question at a time, chosen by priority and by what is still unknown, with warm acknowledgements, skip and pause respected and remembered) and shows what it learned as a CV-like card. The plan (sections, fields, priorities, sensitivity, question phrasings) is in kb.sop; answers are read with patterns, lexicons and the rules of understand.mjs; nothing is sent anywhere and the Profile tab keeps the data in this browser only. Sensitive topics are never asked for and kept only when the user says remember. State lives in ctx.state; the tab renders it. Hand-built platform fixture, not produced by the C1 workflow."
